1 Kor 15,24b-26 Βασιλείαν ὧδε λέγει τοὺς βασιλευομένους, ἤτοι τὴν ἰδίαν σάρκα ἣν
βελτιῶσαι ὁ υἱὸς παρέδωκε τῷ πατρί, οὐκέτι βασιλευομένην ὡς δούλου μορφὴν ἀλλ' ὡς οὖσαν σάρκα τοῦ λόγου ὃ ἔστιν αὐτοῦ τοῦ υἱοῦ, ἀναδείξας τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ μορφὴν ἐν αὐτῇ. τότε γὰρ ἀπειληφότος τοῦ υἱοῦ τὴν δόξαν ἣν εἶχε πρὸ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι, ὡς ὑφ' ἑνὸς βασιλέως πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ βασιλευθήσονται. δεῖ οὖν τὸν Χριστὸν βασιλεύειν ὑπὲρ τῆς ὅλων προκοπῆς ἕως οὗ πάντες οἱ διὰ τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐχθροὶ ὑπὸ πόδας αὐτοῦ τιθῶσιν, καταλύοντος αὐτοῦ πᾶσαν τυραννικὴν ἐξουσίαν, μεθ' ἣν καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ ἀρχίκακος καταλύεται θάνατος, ἐπείπερ πᾶσα ἑνουμένη αὐτῷ ψυχὴ ὑφισταμένη θάνατον τὸν ἑνούμενον τῇ κακίᾳ. 1 Kor 15,27-28 Πρός τε τὴν Ἑλλήνων μυθολογίαν τε καὶ ἀπάτην εἰρῆσθαι ταῦτα εἰπόντες τῶν φασκόντων πατραλοίας εἶναι θεούς, καὶ ὅτι τῆς ἐκκλησίας ὑποτασσομένης αὐτὸς λέγεται ὑποτάττεσθαι, οἰκειούμενος τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοὺς διωγμοὺς καὶ τὰ πάθη καὶ τὴν ὑποταγήν. 1 Kor 15,29 Οἱ ἀπὸ Μαρκίωνος ἀντὶ ἀφωτίστων τεθνεώτων βαπτίζουσι ζῶντας, οὐκ εἰδότες ὅτι τὸ βάπτισμα σώζει μόνον τὸν εἰληφότα αὐτό. ὁ δὲ ἀπόστολος νεκροὺς λέγει τὰ σώματα ὑπὲρ ὧν βαπτιζόμεθα· τῷ γὰρ ἰδίῳ λόγῳ ἄνευ ψυχῆς οὐ ζῇ ταῦτα, ἀλλ' ἐκ τῶν συνουσῶν ψυχῶν ἔχει τὸ ζῆν. ὅμως καὶ ὁ Ἀβραὰμ τὸ ἄψυχον σῶμα νεκρὸν ὠνόμασεν. 1 Kor 15,30 Εἰ μὴ ἀθάνατος ἡ ψυχή, εἰ μὴ ἐγείρεται τὸ σῶμα, εἰ καὶ μάταιον τὸ κινδυνεύειν ὑπὲρ εὐσεβείας. 1 Kor 15,32 Ὅσον κατ' ἀνθρώπινον ἧκε λογισμόν, ἐθηριομάχησα ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἐγὼ οὐκ ἂν ὑποστῆναι τοῦτο βουληθεὶς ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας, εἰ–νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται. 9 1 Kor 15,33 Μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ὦ Κορίνθιοι, ὡς μὴ ἐπιδιαμενούσης τῆς λογικῆς ψυχῆς· οἱ γὰρ ἀπατῶντες ὑμᾶς συμφθείρονται αὐτὴν φθείρεσθαι οἰόμενοι. ᾧ περίκειται σώματα, φασὶν ὅτι σπαταλητέον· αὔριον γὰρ ἀποθνήσκομεν, οὐκ οὔσης ἑτέρας ζωῆς παρὰ τὴν φαινομένην, ὡς τὰ ἄλογα ζῶα ὧν συναφανίζεται ἡ ψυχὴ τῷ σώματι, ἐπειδὴ καὶ συνεσπάρη αὐτῷ. οὐκ ἀνεκτέον οὖν τῶν φαύλων διαλέξεων φθειρουσῶν εὐήθων τὰς γνώμας. 1 Kor 15,34 Γρηγορητέον κατὰ τὴν νόησιν ἵνα μὴ ἁμαρτάνειν συμβῇ ἐν τῷ συγκατατίθεσθαι τῇ σαθρᾷ περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἀπάτῃ. καλῶς δὲ καὶ τὸ ἐκνήψατε δικαίως ὡς μὴ πάντων τοῦτο ποιούντων· οἱ γὰρ σοφοὶ τοῦ κακοποιῆσαι ἀγρυπνοῦντες περὶ τὰ βλαβερὰ ἀδίκως ἐκνήφουσιν ἀποβαλόντες δῆθεν τὸν τῆς ἀμαθίας ὕπνον. 1 Kor 15,35-40 Ὁ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλῶν τῷ ἀμφιβάλλοντι περὶ τῆς τῶν νεκρῶν ἀναστάσεως ὡς ἀσυνέτως φησίν· ἄφρων, εἰ ἀμφιβάλλεις ὅτι τὸ νεκρωθὲν ἀνθρώπου σῶμα ἐγείρεται, ἴσθι ὅτι ἃ σπείρεις σπέρματα ἀποθανόντα εἰς τὴν γὴν καταβάλλεις πεπεισμένος ὡς οὐκ ἂν μεταβάλλοι εἰς φυτά, εἰ μὴ νεκρωθέντα σπαρείη. Ἕτερόν ἐστι τὸ ἐγειρόμενον σῶμα παρ' ὃ ἔσπειρας· σὺ μὲν γὰρ κόκκον ἔβαλες εἰς τὴν γήν, ὁ δὲ θεὸς στάχυν ἤγειρεν. πρὸς μίαν δὲ τῶν ἐρωτήσεων τὴν λέγουσαν πῶς ἐγείρονται νεκροί, ὁ περὶ τῶν σπειρομένων λόγος· πρὸς δὲ τὸ ἕτερον ἐρώτημα, τὸ ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται, ἐκ διαιρέσεως ἀποδίδωσι τὴν ἀπόδειξιν, καὶ διελὼν τὰ σώματα εἰς ἐπίγεια καὶ ἐπουράνια εἶπε κατὰ τὴν τῶν ἐπουρανίων ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης καὶ ἄστρων εἶναι τὴν τῶν ἐγειρομένων ἀνθρωπίνων σωμάτων δόξαν. 1 Kor 15,41 Ὅμοιοι τῇ τῶν φωστήρων καὶ ἀστέρων δόξῃ, οὐ πάντων τῶν ἀνισταμένων τὰ σώματα, ἀλλ' ἢ μόνον τῶν εὖ βεβιωκότων καὶ σωφρονισάντων· κἂν γὰρ τὰ τῶν φαύλων σώματα ἄφθαρτα ἐγείρονται, ἀλλ' οὖν στεροῦνται τῆς τῶν ἐπουρανίων δόξης. σημειωτέον δὲ ὅτι· ἡ δόξα τῶν ἐγειρομένων σωμάτων οὐσιώδης ἐστὶν ὡς καὶ ἡ τῶν φωστήρων. 10 1 Kor 15,42-43 Ὥσπερ ἡ λογικὴ ψυχὴ οὐκ οὖσα ἀρετὴ ἢ κακία δεκτικὴ ἀμφοτέρων ἐστὶ τούτων, οὕτω καὶ τὸ ἡμέτερον σῶμα οὐ φθορὰ ἢ ἀφθαρσία τυγχάνον δέχεται κατὰ διαφόρους χρόνους τὰς ἐγκειμένας οὐσιώδεις ποιότητας. 2 ἀμέλει γοῦν οὐ φθορὰ σπείρεται καὶ ἐγείρεται οὐκ ἀφθαρσία, ἀλλ' ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ. ἀκολουθεῖ δὲ τῷ ἐν φθορᾷ σπειρομένῳ τὸ ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ καὶ ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ καὶ σῶμα ψυχικὸν σπείρεσθαι, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ τῷ ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ ἐγειρομένῳ τὸ ἐν δυνάμει καὶ δόξῃ καὶ σῶμα πνευματικὸν ἐγείρεσθαι.
english: Here Paul calls the kingdom the ones being ruled—that is, his own flesh, which the Son handed over to the Father to improve it, no longer being ruled in the form of a servant but as being the flesh of the Word, which is the Son himself, having displayed the form of God in it. For then, when the Son has received back the glory he had before the world existed, they will be ruled by one king, the Father and the Son. Christ must therefore reign for the advancement of all, until all who are enemies because of sinning are placed under his feet, while he destroys every tyrannical authority. After that, death itself, the arch-evil one, is also destroyed, since every soul united to it undergoes death, which is united to wickedness.

Some say these words were spoken against Greek mythology and deception—against those who claim the gods are father-killers—and that when the church is subjected, he himself is said to be subjected, appropriating to himself the persecutions, the sufferings, and the subjection of the church.

The Marcionites baptize living people on behalf of unillumined dead people, not knowing that baptism saves only the one who receives it. But the apostle calls the bodies dead on behalf of which we are baptized; for by their own nature, without a soul, these do not live, but they have life from the souls that are present with them. Likewise Abraham also called the soulless body dead.
If the soul is not immortal, if the body is not raised, even if risking danger for the sake of piety is futile.
As far as human reasoning goes, I fought with wild beasts in Ephesus; I would not have endured this for the truth, if the dead are not raised.

Do not be deceived, Corinthians, as though the rational soul does not endure. For those who deceive you corrupt others along with themselves, thinking that it is destroyed. Since bodies are wrapped around it, they say one must live luxuriously: for tomorrow we die, since there is no other life besides the visible one, as with irrational animals whose soul is destroyed together with the body, because it was sown together with it. So the worthless arguments that corrupt the minds of the simple must not be tolerated.

We must keep watch in our understanding, so that we do not happen to sin by consenting to the rotten deception about the resurrection. And "sober up" is well said—rightly so—since not all do this. For those who are clever at doing evil stay awake over harmful things and sober up unjustly, supposedly casting off the sleep of ignorance.

The one speaking in Christ says to the one doubting about the resurrection of the dead, as to one who is unintelligent: Fool, if you doubt that the dead body of a human being is raised, know that the seeds you sow you cast into the ground dead, convinced that they would not change into plants unless sown dead. The body that is raised is different from the one you sowed: you cast a grain into the ground, but God raised up an ear of wheat. The argument about seeds answers one of the questions—the one that says, how are the dead raised? To the other question, with what kind of body do they come, he gives the proof by division, and dividing bodies into earthly and heavenly, he said that the glory of the raised human bodies is according to that of the heavenly sun, moon, and stars.

Like the glory of the lights and stars are not the bodies of all who are raised, but only those of the ones who have lived well and been self-controlled. For even if the bodies of the wicked are raised incorruptible, they are nevertheless deprived of the glory of the heavenly bodies. And it must be noted that the glory of the raised bodies is essential, just as is that of the lights.

Just as the rational soul, not being virtue or vice, is receptive of both of these, so also our body, not being corruption or incorruptibility, receives at different times the essential qualities that are placed in it. At any rate, it is not sown as corruption, nor is it raised as incorruptibility, but it is raised in incorruptibility. To what is sown in corruption follows being sown in weakness and dishonor and as a natural body; likewise, what is raised in incorruptibility corresponds to what is raised in power and glory and as a spiritual body.

findings.checker_says: Greek means 'they corrupt themselves, thinking it [the soul] is destroyed', not 'corrupt others'.
findings.reviewer_note: symphtheirontai is middle/passive ("perish/are corrupted together"); neither "corrupt others along with themselves" nor the checker's "corrupt themselves" is clearly right.

findings.quote: Since bodies are wrapped around it
findings.checker_says: ᾧ refers to the soul (feminine), but περίκειται σώματα is neuter plural; the heretics speak, not Didymus explaining.
findings.reviewer_note: English already reports this as the heretics' saying ("they say"); the proposed fix only adds quote marks. The relative ho is loose in the Greek anyway.

findings.quote: Like the glory of the lights and stars are not the bodies of all who are raised
findings.source_quote: Ὅμοιοι τῇ τῶν φωστήρων καὶ ἀστέρων δόξῃ, οὐ πάντων τῶν ἀνισταμένων τὰ σώματα
findings.checker_says: Ὅμοιοι is nominative plural masculine, referring to people: 'Those who are like the glory... are not the bodies of all...' or 'Like the glory... are [those] not of all...'
findings.reviewer_note: Masculine homoioi agreeing loosely with neuter somata; the English says exactly what Didymus says (not all raised bodies share the stars' glory).

findings.quote: it is not sown as corruption, nor is it raised as incorruptibility, but it is raised in incorruptibility
findings.source_quote: οὐ φθορὰ σπείρεται καὶ ἐγείρεται οὐκ ἀφθαρσία, ἀλλ' ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ
findings.checker_says: Missing καὶ before ἐγείρεται; 'corruption is sown and it is raised not as incorruptibility but in incorruptibility'.
findings.reviewer_note: English is right: "it is not sown as corruption, nor raised as incorruption, but in incorruption"; checker invents "corruption is sown".

findings.quote: I would not have endured this for the truth, if the dead are not raised
findings.source_quote: οὐκ ἂν ὑποστῆναι τοῦτο βουληθεὶς ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας, εἰ–νεκροὶ οὐκ ἐγείρονται
findings.checker_says: οὐκ ἂν... βουληθεὶς = 'I would not have wished to endure this'—the Greek has a crux with εἰ–, but 'wished' is missing.
findings.reviewer_note: Counterfactual kept; dropping "willing" (boulethheis) loses only a shade. Optional polish: "I would not have chosen to endure this".

findings.quote: they will be ruled by one king, the Father and the Son
findings.source_quote: ὡς ὑφ' ἑνὸς βασιλέως πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ βασιλευθήσονται
findings.checker_says: Source says 'as by one king, Father and Son'; 'one king, the Father and the Son' misreads the genitive as apposition.
findings.reviewer_note: Same meaning (one king, Father and Son); the referee's "two kings" claim is unfounded.

findings.quote: since every soul united to it undergoes death, which is united to wickedness
findings.source_quote: ἐπείπερ πᾶσα ἑνουμένη αὐτῷ ψυχὴ ὑφισταμένη θάνατον τὸν ἑνούμενον τῇ κακίᾳ
findings.checker_says: Source says 'every soul united to it subsists/constitutes the death united to wickedness'; 'undergoes death' misreads ὑφισταμένη.
findings.reviewer_note: Participial clause has no finite verb and auto may be death or Christ; hyphistamene could be "undergoes" or "withstands". Checker's "constitutes" is unlikely.

findings.quote: even if risking danger for the sake of piety is futile
findings.source_quote: εἰ καὶ μάταιον τὸ κινδυνεύειν ὑπὲρ εὐσεβείας
findings.checker_says: Source says 'if even risking danger for piety is in vain'; 'even if' makes it concessive, but source is conditional.
findings.reviewer_note: Without an apodosis the English sentence is a fragment; the sense (cf. 1 Cor 15:30) is "if the soul is not immortal and the body not raised, then risking danger for piety is futile". Proposed fix keeps the fragment.

findings.quote: And "sober up" is well said—rightly so—since not all do this.
findings.source_quote: καλῶς δὲ καὶ τὸ ἐκνήψατε δικαίως ὡς μὴ πάντων τοῦτο ποιούντων
findings.checker_says: Source says 'sober up' is well said 'rightly, since not all do this'; '—rightly so—' misplaces δικαίως as parenthetical.
findings.reviewer_note: Punctuation preference only; dikaios placement does not change meaning.

findings.quote: as to one who is unintelligent
findings.checker_says: Source says 'as one without understanding' (adverbial); 'as to one who is unintelligent' shifts from manner to person.
findings.reviewer_note: hos asynetos introduces the address "Fool"; "as to one who is unintelligent" is a fair rendering.
